question: When nested transaction.atomic() blocks exit, what has actually committed, what can still roll back, and when do transaction.on_commit() callbacks run?

included: One Django database connection and alias on the ordinary path where autocommit is initially enabled.
Outermost and nested transaction.atomic() entry and exit.
Default savepoint behavior and the savepoint=False branch.
Connection-local transaction.on_commit() registration, pruning, and execution.
Django tests that compare committed rows with callback execution.
excluded: Documentation prose, provider output, and target execution.
Manual transaction management with autocommit already disabled.
Durable-block nesting, broken connections, commit failures, and backend-specific SQL.
Cross-database atomicity, two-phase commit, replication, and task-queue delivery.
A guarantee about filesystem, controller, or device persistence.

facts.statement: With autocommit initially enabled, the outer block disables autocommit; a nested default block creates a savepoint while savepoint=False records no local savepoint.
When block bodies exit without error, nested __exit__ releases its savepoint while outer __exit__ calls connection.commit() before cleanup and callback execution.
An error rolls back a real savepoint when present; without one the inner exit marks the enclosing atomic scope for rollback, and rollback waits for the nearest real enclosing boundary.
The ordinary outermost cleanup restores autocommit after the commit or rollback branch.
A successful connection commit arms queued hooks for the later autocommit transition; rollback clears the whole queue.
Rolling back a savepoint removes callbacks whose registration snapshot contains that savepoint ID; releasing a savepoint does not run them.
Inside an atomic block, on_commit stores the callback with the set of active savepoint IDs; outside a transaction in autocommit mode, it executes immediately.
set_autocommit(True) updates backend and connection state before running and clearing the armed callback queue.
Django tests keep callbacks silent through nested success and observe them only after the outer block commits.

Django tests discard callbacks and rows from rolled-back savepoints, preserve successful siblings, discard everything on outer rollback, and show savepoint=False failure dooming its enclosing transaction scope.
Surviving callbacks run in registration order, are cleared after commit or rollback, and can issue queries or open a fresh atomic block.

claims.title: The ordinary outer block owns the transaction commit
claims.statement: With autocommit initially enabled, entering the outermost atomic block starts Django's transaction boundary and only its no-error __exit__ branch calls connection.commit().
limits: Manual transaction management with autocommit already disabled follows a different ownership path.
The call boundary does not establish backend-specific physical durability.

claims.title: A nested atomic block is usually a savepoint, not a nested commit
claims.statement: A default nested block creates a savepoint, and successful exit releases that savepoint without committing the database transaction.
limits: Backends without usable savepoints are outside this episode.
The method name savepoint_commit means release here, not database transaction commit.

claims.title: Inner success remains provisional until outer success
claims.statement: Rows written and callbacks registered by a successful inner block can still be removed by a later rollback of an enclosing savepoint or the outer transaction.
limits: This statement is scoped to one connection and alias.

claims.title: A failed inner savepoint can be isolated
claims.statement: When a real inner savepoint exists, Django rolls back that scope and discards its callbacks; if the exception is handled outside that block, earlier outer work can continue and commit.
limits: The exception must be handled outside the failed atomic block without masking a broken transaction state.

claims.title: `savepoint=False` removes a recovery boundary, not just overhead
claims.statement: A nested savepoint=False block neither commits nor owns a local rollback point; its failed exit performs no rollback there and propagates needs_rollback until the nearest enclosing real savepoint or outer transaction rolls back.
limits: Callbacks may remain queued until that enclosing boundary actually rolls back; this claim does not say they are removed immediately.

claims.title: `on_commit()` callbacks follow their rollback scope
claims.statement: Registration captures active savepoint IDs, so rollback prunes callbacks from that scope while callbacks from surviving sibling or outer scopes remain queued.
limits: The queue is connection-local and does not coordinate separate database aliases.

claims.title: Surviving callbacks run after commit and autocommit restoration
claims.statement: After the outer body exits without error and commit succeeds, __exit__ restores autocommit and drains surviving callbacks in registration order before returning; callback code can therefore query or start a new transaction.
limits: A non-robust callback exception can stop the remaining local drain, but cannot undo the already successful commit.
Outside a transaction under ordinary autocommit, on_commit executes immediately.

claims.title: Treat `on_commit()` as a post-commit handoff, not a delivery guarantee
claims.statement: The useful design signal is to place side effects after transaction success, while recognizing that this in-process queue supplies no durable retry or crash-recovery contract.
limits: The handoff framing is an engineering interpretation, not a named Django abstraction.
The inspected code does not prove delivery after process failure.

branch_map.trigger: A default nested block exits without error.
branch_map.transaction_effect: Its savepoint is released; all inner and outer writes remain part of the outer transaction.

branch_map.trigger: A nested block with a real savepoint exits through an error.
branch_map.transaction_effect: That savepoint is rolled back; earlier outer writes remain provisional.
branch_map.callback_effect: Callbacks registered under that savepoint are discarded.

branch_map.trigger: A nested savepoint=False block exits through an error.
branch_map.transaction_effect: No rollback occurs at this inner exit; needs_rollback propagates until the nearest real enclosing boundary rolls back.
branch_map.callback_effect: Callbacks cannot run if that enclosing scope rolls back, but they need not be pruned at the inner exit itself.

branch_map.trigger: The ordinary outer block body exits without error and connection.commit() succeeds.
branch_map.transaction_effect: Django restores autocommit inside __exit__ after commit returns.
branch_map.callback_effect: Surviving callbacks drain before __exit__ returns; a non-robust callback can still make the with statement raise.

branch_map.transaction_effect: All work in that transaction is rolled back.
branch_map.callback_effect: The connection callback queue is cleared.

branch_map.trigger: on_commit is called with no atomic block and autocommit enabled.
branch_map.transaction_effect: There is no pending transaction boundary.

uncertainties.statement: The inspected Django boundary does not establish when a specific database makes the commit physically durable or externally replicated.
uncertainties.next_check: Pin one database backend and inspect its driver and server durability contract only if that becomes the user's question.

uncertainties.statement: The in-memory callback queue does not establish delivery if the process exits after database commit but before or during callback execution.
uncertainties.next_check: Inspect an application-level outbox or task delivery path rather than promoting this callback queue into a durable guarantee.
